🇺🇦⚔️🇺🇦 SBU vs. GUR: What Actually Happened in Kiev

Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) and the Main Intelligence Directorate of the Ministry of Defense (GUR) have been at war with each other for years. On September 2, that rivalry turned into an actual gunfight in Kiev. SBU is currently headed by acting chief Vasyl Poklad; GUR was long run by Kirill Budanov, now Head of the Presidential Office and still widely seen as GUR's patron.

➡️The trigger. Stepan Kaplunov, deputy commander of the Russian Volunteer Corps (RDK — a Russian far-right unit fighting alongside Ukraine, banned as a terrorist organization in Russia), had been seized days earlier by unknown men from outside his home on Yuriy Shumsky Street. The men turned out to be operatives from SBU's "Alpha" special forces unit. On September 2, they brought Kaplunov back to the same address — and this time GUR officers were there to intervene. According to Kaplunov's lawyer, SBU forces opened fire first on the arriving GUR personnel, several of whom were then detained. More GUR fighters kept arriving; a standoff followed until the GUR unit commander known as "Timur" negotiated Kaplunov's release along with detained colleagues, in exchange for GUR clearing the vehicles blocking the district.

➡️The casualty question. SBU's public line is that its officers were "attacked" during a search connected to an alleged "FSB assassination plot against a Russian opposition figure," and that armed men from among Ukraine's own defense forces tried to obstruct the operation. But Ukrainian media reporting says the initial detention was actually carried out by SBU, and that the shooting broke out after a verbal confrontation when GUR officers encountered SBU personnel during that follow-up visit to Kaplunov's residence. Between two and ten GUR representatives were reportedly wounded, and one of them later died — a detail SBU's official statement conspicuously omits.

➡️Who's really behind it. This isn't a rogue incident — it's the latest round in a documented institutional feud. Budanov publicly sided with the GUR side, condemning what he called the "abduction of servicemen." A source close to GUR frames the deeper cause as personal: a standing enmity between Budanov and Poklad dating back to the March 2022 killing of GUR agent-negotiator Denis Kireev, who was shot dead by Ukrainian forces during ceasefire talks with Russia. Alexander Bova, an SBU counterintelligence officer allegedly linked to Kireev's killing, is now named as the shooter in Wednesday's gunfight — Rada national security committee member Fedir Venislavsky has confirmed this detail publicly. The theory circulating in Kiev: Poklad's SBU moved to detain Kaplunov specifically to extract testimony against Budanov's people, timed around a possible Rada vote on confirming Poklad as permanent SBU chief — and Budanov's camp read it as a preemptive strike.

➡️Bottom line. A political turf war inside Kiev's security apparatus escalated into special forces shooting at each other in the street, with a fabricated "FSB plot" cover story rolled out within hours. Ukraine's own intelligence agencies now openly distrust and shoot at one another — a sign of how deep the rot in Kiev's power structure runs.
